# Autoresearch: nanoGPT `val_bpb` Optimization

Open-ended optimization of the [karpathy/autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch) nanoGPT pre-training loop. Agents iterate on `repo/train.py` (cloned from upstream by `download_repo.sh`) to drive validation bits-per-byte (`val_bpb`) down indefinitely. There is no wall-clock deadline — the loop runs until stagnation (0 KEEPs in the last 10 experiments) or user interrupt.

## Setup

```bash
bash task-autoresearch/download_repo.sh    # one-time: clones upstream into repo/
```

After cloning, the layout becomes:

```
task-autoresearch/
├── LAUNCH.md           Task profile (runbook hooks for optimization)
├── TASK.md             This file
├── README.md           Setup notes
├── download_repo.sh    Clones karpathy/autoresearch into repo/
├── .gitignore          Excludes repo/ from this repo
└── repo/               karpathy/autoresearch clone (after running download_repo.sh)
    └── train.py        The file the agents evolve
```

## Hardware

2× NVIDIA RTX 4080S (32 GB) — GPU agents run sequentially per device, pinned to `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `=1`.

## Metric

- **`val_bpb`** (validation bits-per-byte): lower is better.
- A result is a KEEP if it strictly improves on the current champion.
- The system stops when the last 10 experiments produced 0 KEEPs.

## Run

```bash
claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-autoresearch. Run name: ar_baseline."
```

# exp_batch_2e16: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 -> 2**16 (DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 -> 32, grad_accum 1)

## Change
`TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17` -> `2**16` and `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 64` -> `32`, keeping width
(ASPECT_RATIO=64, n_embd=512) fixed. grad_accum_steps = 1 in both configs; the change halves
tokens per optimizer step (131,072 -> 65,536) and therefore doubles the step count the 300 s
budget buys, at identical total tokens seen.

## Result
- **val_bpb = 1.094356** (champion 1.094037, delta +0.000319, outcome **DISCARD**)
- num_steps = **1396** (champion 719, +94%); num_params_M = 50.3
- total_tokens = **91.5M** (champion 94.2M -- same tokens, 2x steps)
- training_seconds = 300.1; total_seconds = 374.3; peak_vram_mb = 11549.9
- throughput ~302k tok/s (champion ~308-314k tok/s); MFU (H100-constant, understated) 7.31%

## Training Dynamics
- Block-mean loss: {'0-5': 5.919, '5-20': 4.0, '20-40': 3.566, '40-60': 3.413, '60-80': 3.258, '80-95': 3.128, '95-100.01': 3.083}
- Loss still decreasing through the warmdown tail (3.18 at 80% -> 3.08 at 100%), no plateau.
- Peak VRAM 11.5 GB (vs 22.7 GB at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64) -- batch 32 is very comfortable.
- **2x optimizer steps at fixed width produced no gain** (+0.000319 bpb, inside the 0.003
  conservative noise band). The step lever has flattened between batch 2**17 and 2**16.

## Interpretation
At constant tokens-seen, doubling the number of optimizer steps (halving the batch) is neutral.
Combined with exp_batch_2e17 (2**18 -> 2**17 KEEP, +0.076) this localises the optimum: the big
win came from escaping a large batch (373 steps), but 719 -> 1396 steps adds nothing. The batch
axis appears saturated at 2**17; smaller batches buy steps that no longer convert into quality.
Next high-value moves are NOT further batch halving -- they should be step-neutral quality changes
or the width scale-up probe (exp_aspect_ratio_80).

## Verification
- diff_applied: true (byte-diff vs champion/train.py verified before launch)
- No OOM; exit code 0

- exp_adam_eps_bracket (post d6fdc31d): AdamW eps 1e-10 -> {1e-8, 1e-6} in all five AdamW groups.

1. Killed a tempting proposal with a mechanism check: ns_steps 5->2 is NOT shape-only. NorMuon's
   `final_scale = step_size*(v_norm/v_norm_new)` normalizes to ||X_ns||, and X grows from ~0.98
   toward sqrt(rank) as ns_steps converges, so ns_steps sets update MAGNITUDE. It duplicates the

# Team throughput

## Cycle-4 hypothesis check (Step 0.3)

| result | classification |
|---|---|
| exp_batch_2e17 KEEP (+0.076017, 719 steps, +93%) | SUPPORTS -> supported_keeps 1 |
| exp_batch_2e16 DISCARD (+0.000319, 1396 steps, +94%) | REFUTES -> refuted_discards 1 |
| exp_aspect_ratio_32 DISCARD (-0.008807, 1741 steps, +142% steps but 0.34x width) | REFUTES the step clause, confounded by width -> refuted_discards 2 |
| exp_warmdown_070 DISCARD (seed pair) | orthogonal (step-neutral) |
| exp_ve_all_layers / exp_depth_10 (other teams) | orthogonal (capacity, not steps) |

Formal falsification rule (age>=3 AND supported_keeps==0 AND refuted>=3) does NOT fire because
supported_keeps=1. But **2 of 2 experiments that were pure step increases at fixed width DISCARDed**,
so the stated prediction is dead even though the formal counter is not.

## Reformulated hypothesis (H-throughput-v2)

> At fixed width and ~fixed tokens, what exp_batch_2e17 bought was **proximity to the critical batch
> size**, not "more optimizer steps". 262,144 tokens/update (2**18) was ABOVE the critical batch;
> 131,072 (2**17) is at/below the knee and is where the win stopped. Cutting to 65,536 (2**16) doubled
> updates and returned nothing.

Prediction under v2:
- Further batch/step rungs KEEP nothing. **Do not queue them.**
- Remaining wins are either (a) more tokens at fixed FLOPs (lower FLOPs/token without losing
  capacity), or (b) quality per token (LR / regularization / readout), or (c) higher raw throughput.
- (a) is individually sub-noise: GQA kv4->1 is -7.9% FLOPs -> +8.6% tokens -> ~-0.005; MLP 4->3 is
  -11% FLOPs but -12% MLP capacity. Neither clears the 0.006 band alone.
- (c) is the only change that compounds across every later experiment: at the external scaling-law
  rate (~-0.05 bpb per doubling of tokens), **+10% tokens/s is worth ~0.007 bpb** - more than most
  queued knobs, and it improves every subsequent run.

Falsification for v2: a step/batch change below 2**17 that KEEPs by >0.006, or a >=10% throughput
change that moves val_bpb by less than the seed band.

## Cycle-4 budget audit (Step 1e, corrected)

The code logs `mfu` against `H100_BF16_PEAK_FLOPS = 989.5e12`, which is why every result reports
~7.4% "MFU". That number is meaningless on a 4080S and has been misleading the compute audit.

Corrected: RTX 4080 SUPER BF16 dense with FP32 accumulate ~= 2x FP32 = **~104 TFLOPS**.
Champion FLOPs/token (from estimate_flops): 6*(50.33M - 20.97M excluded) + attention
= 176.2M + 12*512*(6*1024 + 2*2048) = 176.2M + 62.9M = **239.1M**.
At 314k tok/s that is **~75 TFLOPS = ~72% of peak**. Memory: 22,653/32,760 MB = **69.3%**.

Verdict: compute efficiency is ABOVE the 50% line (the earlier "idle capacity" reading was an
artifact of the H100 constant). The run is compute-bound, not memory-bound. The Step-1e scale-up
probe still exists in the queue (exp_aspect_ratio_80, +52% FLOPs/token -> ~473 steps) but it is a
*capacity-for-steps trade*, and both available data points on that trade lost (depth_10 -0.097,
ve_all_layers -0.006 = 2.0 sigma). Read aspect_80 as a falsification probe for H-capacity.

## Cycle-4 queue priorities (throughput team)
1. exp_wd_0p0 (HIGH - raised this cycle): cumulative Muon shrink e^-3.0 ~ 0.05 at 719 steps, i.e. the
   run is discarding ~95% of its weight growth. Largest single mechanism in the team's queue.
2. exp_embedding_tied (new): readout-cold-start fix.
3. exp_softcap_30 (new): Layer-3 literal, closes a ledger row.
4. exp_aspect_ratio_80 (medium): pre-registered falsification probe.
5. exp_unembedding_lr_hi (medium) / _lo (low): readout LR bracket; 3x arms are now known to be
   borderline vs the 0.006 band, so run hi first.

## Acceptance rule
A KEEP requires surviving the multi-seed gate: both seeds strictly beat the champion. With
sigma=0.00302, only |delta| >= ~0.006 is decidable. Do not close an axis on one sub-band sample.

## Derived facts (cycle 4)
- Adam LRs are dim-scaled by 1.2247; MATRIX_LR is NOT dim-scaled. Because NorMuon renormalizes the
  update norm, that asymmetry is defensible, not a bug.
- grad_accum_steps = 2**17 / (64*2048) = 1. 719 steps in 300.4 s (418 ms/step), 94.2M tokens.
- Peak VRAM 22,653 MB = 69.1% of 32,768. Compute efficiency: real MFU ~73% (reported 7.47% is wrong).
  Step 1e: memory is marginally under 70%, but the only batch-side scale-up (DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128)
  OOMs, and the model-side scale-ups (aspect 80, mlp 6) are already queued by other teams.

## Confound note on ns_steps (new this cycle)
`muon_step_fused` computes `final_scale = step_size * (v_norm / v_norm_new)` where `v_norm` is the
Frobenius norm of the **orthogonalized** gradient and `v_norm_new` the norm of the scaled one. The
update therefore has norm exactly `||X_ns||`, and X grows from ~0.98 (normalized input) toward
sqrt(rank) as ns_steps lets the polar iteration converge. So **ns_steps changes the update
MAGNITUDE, not only its shape** - it is a Muon-LR lever in disguise. Do not run it as a "shape-only"
probe while exp_matrix_lr_lo/hi is still pending.

# Team gradient-quality - cycle 4

**Hypothesis (H-gradient-quality):** gradient signal per step is suboptimal.
**Prediction:** changes that reduce gradient noise or improve update direction will KEEP.
**Falsification:** 3 rotations of prediction-consistent experiments all DISCARD.

## Champion state (cycle 4)
`exp_batch_2e17`, val_bpb **1.094037**. DEPTH=8 -> n_embd 512, 4 heads x 128, vocab 8192, seq 2048,
50.3M params. TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, **grad_accum=1**, **719 steps**,
94.2M tokens, ~308-314k tok/s, peak VRAM 22,653 MB (69.1% of 32,768).

## THE cycle-4 fact: the noise floor is 2x the protocol default
Two independent same-code seed pairs now exist (warmdown_070 code: 0.004138; adam_beta2_hi code:
0.004396). Pooled **sigma = 0.00302, 2-sigma = 0.00604**. The old "conservative 0.003 band" is
1 sigma, not 2. Consequences:
- The whole queue's expected effects (0.002-0.008) straddle 2 sigma. 1-seed arms are mostly ties.
- exp_adam_beta2_hi's seed-42 leg beat the champion by 0.000198 (0.07 sigma) and its seed-43 leg
  lost by 0.0042. Without the multi-seed gate that would have been a false KEEP on the champion.
- exp_muon_mom_ramp60 (+0.004053, 1.34 sigma) is re-classified NOISE-CONTAMINATED and the axis is
  re-opened. dead_ends.md and knowledge/noise_floor.md updated.
- **Rule adopted: no KEEP and no axis closure on a 1-seed |delta| < 0.006.** Re-probe far/opposite.

## Result classification (cycle 4)
New since cycle 3:
- `exp_warmdown_070` DISCARD, 2 seeds (1.093748 / 1.097886 vs 1.094037) -> seed mean 0.59 sigma = tie.
  Orthogonal to H (throughput). Warmdown is closed around 0.5: 0.25 is worse (2.2 sigma), 0.7 is a tie.
- `exp_adam_beta2_hi` DISCARD, 2 seeds -> the first H-gradient-quality experiment to complete.
  Classified **REFUTES the beta2 arm specifically** (taking the second-moment horizon from 20 to
  100 steps did not help), but it does NOT refute "reduce update noise" as a principle: 0.99 is one
  point on one moment. Counters therefore go to refuted_discards=2 (warmup, muon ramp) and beta2 is
  recorded as a beta2-specific negative, not a third refutation of the hypothesis.
- Counters: age_rotations=3, supported_keeps=0, refuted_discards=2.
  **Not falsified** (falsification needs refuted >= 3). One more refuting result triggers
  [HYPOTHESIS-FALSIFIED].

## Why the hypothesis is still alive but under pressure
1. Step count saturated (719 -> 1396 steps bought +0.0003). The remaining value must come from
   per-update progress - which is exactly H's claim - but that window is now narrow.
2. Everything the team has tested on the AdamW side (beta2) and the momentum side (ramp) is inside
   noise or negative. The two untested members of the same family are **adam beta1** (queued) and
   **AdamW eps** (filed this cycle). If both come back flat, H-gradient-quality is in serious trouble.
3. A weak but real alternative reading of the data: the binding constraint may be the **LR schedule
   shape at fixed 300 s**, not gradient quality. warmdown 0.25 losing 2.2 sigma is the only schedule
   point outside the band, and it says "decay longer, not shorter".

## Cycle-4 proposals (this analyst)
1. `exp_adam_eps_bracket` -> ADAMW eps 1e-10 -> {1e-8, 1e-6}. Axis `adam_eps`, direction increase.
   Never proposed by anyone; 5 AdamW groups = 50% of params; 1e-10 is 100x below torch's default and

- `ns_steps 5 -> 2`: looks like a shape-only update-direction probe, but NorMuon's `final_scale`

- Any small-width / small-depth arm, any batch rung, any second unembedding_lr bracket (duplicate

## Exchange rate - RETRACTED and replaced
The cycle-2 claim "-0.00027 val_bpb per +1% optimizer steps" is NOT supported. Updates per run:
193 -> 373 -> 719 -> 1396; val_bpb 1.195701 -> 1.170054 -> 1.094037 -> 1.094356. That is
non-monotone: the second doubling bought 3x what the first did, the third bought ZERO. A smooth
step-count law cannot produce that. The correct reading:

**The batch ladder was a critical-batch-size traversal, not a step lever.**
- 262,144 tokens/update (2**18) is ABOVE the critical batch: tokens were spent on redundant
  gradient estimates. Cut to 131,072 -> -0.076.
- 131,072 (2**17) is AT/below the knee: cutting to 65,536 (2**16) bought 2x updates and returned
  nothing (+0.0003).
So the winning property of exp_batch_2e17 is "the update is at the critical batch", and it is now
saturated. Do not spend slots on further batch/step rungs.

## Tokens->loss rate (the number we still do NOT have)
Every ladder run held tokens ~constant (91.5-97.8M), so none of the 11 experiments cleanly measures
d(loss)/d(tokens) at fixed width. aspect_ratio_32 (228M tokens at 0.34x params) is confounded by
capacity. A planning estimate from external scaling laws (~-0.05 bpb per doubling at this size)
implies a +10% throughput gain is worth ~0.007 bpb - i.e. ONE throughput change is worth more than
most queued knobs, and is the only kind of change that compounds across every later experiment.

# exp_batch_2e18 — halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18

## Experiment (H-throughput)
Halve the optimizer-step token budget: `TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**19 -> 2**18`.
`DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE` stays 64, so `grad_accum_steps` goes 4 -> 2 and the fixed
300 s wall-clock budget accommodates ~2x as many optimizer updates.

## Result
- val_bpb = **1.170054** vs champion 1.195701  ->  **delta +0.025647** (lower is better)
- **KEEP** (delta is 8.5x the conservative 2-sigma band of 0.003; no measured seed
  variance exists yet in knowledge/noise_floor_data.md, so the conservative default
  was used. Delta is far outside it — no second seed required.)
- num_steps 193 -> 373, training_seconds 300.4, peak_vram_mb 22805.5 (unchanged)

## Training Dynamics
- **num_steps: 373** vs 193 at champion (1.93x). total_tokens_M 97.8 (essentially the same
  token budget; the gain is purely from optimizer-step count, not extra data).
- **dt per step: 830 ms** vs 1651 ms — exactly halved, as expected from halving tokens/step.
  tok/s unchanged (~315.6k vs 317.5k), i.e. no throughput loss from the smaller batch.
- **Still decreasing at end:** loss 3.41 at 80% -> 3.27 at 99.8% (drop 0.14, same absolute
  late-training slope as the baseline). The model remains undertrained even at 373 steps:
  more steps should still help, so the axis is NOT exhausted at this point.
- **No early plateau.** Loss falls monotonically; the smaller batch did not destabilize.
- Smoothed train loss at end: 3.273 vs 3.365 at champion — consistent with the val_bpb gain.

## Interpretation
This is the cleanest confirmation of H-throughput: identical tokens/sec, identical
memory, identical model, only the number of optimizer updates changed — and val_bpb
improved by 0.0256. The run is step-starved, not data-starved.

  the champion (~75.6 TFLOP/s). The step loss comes from model size, not from the

  steps. The loss gap is consistent with the step deficit.

regime. The capacity gain (+71% params) is outweighed by the 41% loss of optimizer

count dominates at ~200-700 steps. The paired low probe (exp_depth_6, still queued)

# exp_muon_beta2_hi: NorMuon beta2 0.95 -> 0.99

## Experiment
Single unconditional literal change in `setup_optimizer()`'s Muon param-group dict:
`momentum=0.95, ns_steps=5, beta2=0.95` -> `beta2=0.99`. The dict is built once per matrix
shape, so all Muon groups (25.17M params = 50% of the model, basically all per-token FLOPs)
are affected. `ADAM_BETAS` and the x0 group `(0.96,0.95)` untouched. Proposal c093a9b1.

NorMuon's beta2 is the EMA horizon of the **row-wise variance** used to rescale the
orthogonalized update. 0.95 = 20-step horizon (2.8% of a 719-step run) -> 0.99 = 100-step
horizon (14%). Because `final_scale = step_size * v_norm / v_norm_new` cancels the magnitude,
this is a pure direction/noise knob, not a step-size knob.

## Result
- **val_bpb: 1.094608** vs champion 1.094037 (exp_batch_2e17)
- delta (ours - champion): **+0.000571** = 0.19 sigma under the measured seed sigma 0.00302
  -> **statistical TIE, inside the noise band**
- Outcome: **DISCARD** (not a near-miss; inside band)
- Steps 718, tokens 94.1M, ~308k tok/s, peak VRAM 22,653 MB, training 300.4 s — step-neutral as designed
- Race condition: False (champion v5 unchanged)

## Training Dynamics
Train loss vs the champion run (same seed 42, same data order) is indistinguishable:
| progress | ours | champion | diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20% | 3.8145 | 3.8174 | -0.0029 |
| 40% | 3.4902 | 3.4902 | +0.0000 |
| 60% | 3.3108 | 3.3063 | +0.0045 |
| 80% | 3.1640 | 3.1639 | +0.0000 |
| 99% | 3.0709 | 3.0663 | +0.0046 |
Final *train* loss is marginally lower (3.0680 vs 3.0726) while val_bpb is marginally higher
(+0.00057) — both directions inside noise. Loss is still falling at the end (-0.093 over the
final 20%), i.e. the run remains undertrained; no early plateau.

## Interpretation (for analysts)
Together with exp_adam_beta2_hi (beta2 0.99 on AdamW: +0.0002, 0.07 sigma) this closes the
"second-moment / variance horizon" family on **both** optimizers as inert at this step budget.
H-gradient-quality's noise-reduction half now has three independent null results
(Adam beta2, NorMuon beta2, embedding LR hi tie). The remaining gradient-quality levers are
first-moment (beta1) and the learning-rate magnitudes themselves; structural/init changes are
the better use of slots than finer EMA tuning.

# exp_head_dim_64 — HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64 (head granularity at fixed width)

- agent: ar_20261022hi_gpu5 (team capacity, GPU 0)
- axis: head_dim | direction: decrease | value: 64 (from 128)
- baseline: champion exp_batch_2e17 = 1.094037 (val_bpb, minimize)
- **result: val_bpb = 1.100821  -> delta +0.006784  (2.25 sigma, 2-sigma band 0.00604)**
- **outcome: DISCARD** (real regression, outside the 2-sigma band)

## What changed
One line, unconditional: `HEAD_DIM = 128` -> `HEAD_DIM = 64` (train.py:434).
`build_model_config(8)` gives base_dim = 8*64 = 512, already a multiple of 64, so n_embd stays 512 and
HEAD_DIM only sets attention granularity: **n_head 4 -> 8, head_dim 128 -> 64**.

## Verification that the probe was clean
| quantity | champion | this run |
|---|---|---|
| n_layer / n_embd | 8 / 512 | 8 / 512 |
| n_head (n_kv_head) | 4 (4) | **8 (8)** |
| total params | 50,332,688 | 50,332,688 (identical) |
| FLOPs/token | 2.3908e8 | 2.3908e8 (identical) |
| num_steps | 719 | 725 (+0.8%, jitter) |
| total_tokens_M | 94.2 | 95.0 |
| peak_vram_mb | 22653 | 22702 |
| training_seconds | 300.4 | 300.2 |

So the throughput confound that makes every depth/width probe uninterpretable is absent here:
this is a pure per-step representational difference at fixed params, fixed FLOPs, fixed steps.

## Training Dynamics
- Loss is still decreasing at the end: mean loss over steps 95-100% = 3.0978 vs 3.1161 over 90-95%
  (slope ~ -5.2e-4/step over the last 10%). Undertrained at 725 steps, same as champion.
- Loss at 50% was 3.4234 (from 6.14 at step 1); no early plateau -> capacity is not the binding limit.
- **Early-training penalty is large and monotonically decaying** (vs the team's ve_all run, same width):
  | step | head_dim_64 | ve_all (4/8 VE) | diff |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 100 | 4.4370 | 4.1145 | +0.3225 |
  | 200 | 3.6681 | 3.6139 | +0.0541 |
  | 400 | 3.4008 | 3.3835 | +0.0173 |
  | 600 | 3.1720 | 3.1612 | +0.0107 |
  | 700 | 3.1098 | 3.1036 | +0.0062 |

## Interpretation
Eight 64-dim heads are **worse than four 128-dim heads at identical parameter count and FLOPs**, and the
damage is concentrated early: the run starts ~0.32 nats behind at step 100 and only closes to ~+0.004 by
the end of the 300 s budget. Two readings, both consistent with the step-saturated regime:
1. Narrower heads have a slower optimization transient (more heads = more independent score distributions
   to fit; RoPE rotates 32 pairs/head instead of 64, so the lowest frequency presented to each head is
   halved on the long-window layers).
2. In a fixed 300 s budget the early transient is exactly what you cannot afford to pay. Even if the
   asymptotic gap were zero, the run would still lose ~0.007 val_bpb because it spends its limited
   steps recovering.

This is a **per-step-quality** result, not a step-count result: steps were identical (+0.8%), so it
cannot be explained by throughput.

## Followup
- The opposite arm (HEAD_DIM 128 -> 256, n_head 2) is unrun. If the monotone read above is right,
  256 should be better, not worse — that would be the informative opposite probe, and it is also
  zero-param / zero-FLOPs.
- `head_dim=64` (direction=decrease) should NOT be re-probed; it is 2.25 sigma worse.

# Autoresearch: nanoGPT `val_bpb` Optimization

Open-ended optimization of the [karpathy/autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch) nanoGPT pre-training loop. Agents iterate on `repo/train.py` (cloned from upstream by `download_repo.sh`) to drive validation bits-per-byte (`val_bpb`) down indefinitely. There is no wall-clock deadline — the loop runs until stagnation (0 KEEPs in the last 10 experiments) or user interrupt.

## Setup

```bash
bash task-autoresearch/download_repo.sh    # one-time: clones upstream into repo/
```

After cloning, the layout becomes:

```
task-autoresearch/
├── LAUNCH.md           Task profile (runbook hooks for optimization)
├── TASK.md             This file
├── README.md           Setup notes
├── download_repo.sh    Clones karpathy/autoresearch into repo/
├── .gitignore          Excludes repo/ from this repo
└── repo/               karpathy/autoresearch clone (after running download_repo.sh)
    └── train.py        The file the agents evolve
```

## Hardware

2× NVIDIA RTX 4080S (32 GB) — GPU agents run sequentially per device, pinned to `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0` and `=1`.

## Metric

- **`val_bpb`** (validation bits-per-byte): lower is better.
- A result is a KEEP if it strictly improves on the current champion.
- The system stops when the last 10 experiments produced 0 KEEPs.

## Run

```bash
claude -p "Read runbook.md and execute. Task: task-autoresearch. Run name: ar_baseline."
```

# Capacity audit: depth/width coupling and the true param budget

## Correction: the model is ~50M params, not ~126M
`GPTConfig(vocab_size=32768)` is a default that is always overridden in `build_model_config(vocab_size=tokenizer.get_vocab_size())`. The shipped tokenizer has **8192** tokens (`prepare.py` `VOCAB_SIZE=8192`, incl. 4 specials). Correct decomposition at champion (DEPTH=8, ASPECT_RATIO=64 -> model_dim=512):

| component | params |
|---|---|
| transformer blocks (8 x 3.146M) | 25.17M |
| value embeddings (4 layers x 8192*512) | 16.78M |
| token embedding wte | 4.19M |
| lm_head | 4.19M |
| resid/x0 scalars | 16 |
| **total** | **50.33M** |

## The depth/width coupling
`model_dim = DEPTH * ASPECT_RATIO`, rounded up to a multiple of `HEAD_DIM`. So `DEPTH = 12` alone (AR still 64) gives model_dim=768 and 135.3M params (+169%) -- a depth+width+FLOPs compound change. To test depth alone, co-adjust AR:

| config | width | params | delta vs champion |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEPTH=6, AR=85 | 512 | 39.85M | -20.8% |
| DEPTH=8, AR=64 (champion) | 512 | 50.33M | 0 |
| DEPTH=12, AR=42 | 512 | 71.30M | +41.7% |

This is the bracket queued as `exp_cap_depth12_w512` / `exp_cap_depth6_w512`.

## Value embeddings dominate depth scaling
`has_ve(i, n_layer)` is parity-based (`i % 2 == (n_layer-1) % 2`). n_layer=8 -> VE on 4 layers; n_layer=12 -> VE on 6 layers; n_layer=6 -> VE on 3. Each VE is 8192*512 = 4.19M params, i.e. **more than the 3.15M transformer-block cost added by one layer**. Therefore:
- depth 8->12 adds 4 blocks (12.58M) + 2 VEs (8.39M) = +20.97M.
- A VE-count change is a first-class capacity dial: 8 VEs = +16.78M (+33%); 2 VEs = -8.39M (-17%).

## Baseline memory risk (flag for GPU agents)
At DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128, the final logits are [128, 2048, 8192]: 4.29GB bf16, 8.59GB after the explicit `.float()`; saved MLP intermediates are ~64*2048*2048*2 = 0.54GB (fc out) + 0.54GB (relu-square out) per layer, ~8.6GB over 8 layers at batch 64. At batch 128 activation memory roughly doubles to ~17GB, on top of ~8.6GB logits + ~2GB weights/optimizer -> ~28-30GB, right at the 32GB limit. **Recommended memory-safe baseline: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**19 (grad_accum=4) so optimizer-step semantics are unchanged.** Do not attribute a batch-64 baseline to the TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE axis; that is a micro-batch/memory change only.

## MFU reporting caveat
`H100_BF16_PEAK_FLOPS = 989.5e12` is hardcoded and used as the MFU denominator. On 2x RTX 4080S (~1/10 of that dense bf16 peak) `mfu_percent` is understated by roughly an order of magnitude. When applying the compute-budget audit rule, do not read the printed MFU as real utilization; use wall-clock step count and tokens/sec instead.

because the decay has been switched off.

2%-of-run EMA horizon) and still could not produce a measurable final metric — **not because the
coefficient is small but because the schedule annihilates it before the evaluation point.** Any future
regularization proposal on this code should check whether its schedule zeroes the term before the end
of the run; a knob that is off for the last 50% cannot move a final-state metric by much.
